summary: D14 (ckpt) survives every test I could put to it. D13 (fabric) survives in its conclusion and FAILS on its evidence. The fixer's blocking premise really is false: all four constructors are literal in the frozen old tree at exactly the cited lines, inside Fabric.__init__ (self_organize.py:1636). state_dict's list and build's allocation now agree name for name in BOTH directions -- 10 names, 20 tensors, no orphan, no gap -- and a payload round-trip through CKPT.load loses nothing. But the ground D13 records for DROPPING q_entry is wrong on the facts. It says q_entry has 'exactly three readers' and that :2597 is 'the else of if s.halt_on, on that same non-grounded branch'. There are six reader sites, not three (:2320 is an unlisted forward-path read the ruling never mentions), and :2597 is NOT on the non-grounded branch: the `_hlg` assignment sits at the same indent as `if s.grounded:` and is evaluated on BOTH branches, gated only on `s.halt_on` -- i.e. FAB_HALT, which .rework/census.json verdicts KEEP and which src/fabric/api.py::build reads and records as fab.halt. So one of q_entry's readers is reached at the grounded default on the ported soc walk whenever FAB_HALT=0, which is exactly the condition the brief said would sink the ruling. The conclusion nevertheless survives, on an argument the ruling never made and which I had to establish myself: on the soc walk the pre-loop entry distribution `c` reaches nothing but ground_update, ground_update renormalises its weights (`_share = _iv / _iv.sum()` at self_organize.py:2414), and the soc branch returns before `c` is used again -- so q_entry's value has no gradient path and no numerical effect on the ported walk at either halt setting. The right reason is 'the entry distribution is dead on the soc walk', not 'its readers are on dropped arms'. Two further evidence faults: the old tree's 'never gradiented -> ctrl, q_entry' audit (self_organize.py:9141, loop at :7085) was measured at the shipped FAB_HALT=1 and cannot be extended to FAB_HALT=0; and the two .rework/ISSUES.md records cited as 1594-1595 and 1789-1790 are not those records (they are P3-C26 and P3-H28) -- the real ones are P3-C28 at 1602-1604 and P3-H30 at 1797-1799. D14: type is still exactly units.Windows, both spine/compose.py call sites work (I ran compose._periods and got Windows(4000) carrying ckpt.periodic_armed), all four CKPT_DIR x CKPT_EVERY corners print four distinguishable honest states, and the dir-unset case is correctly UNREACHABLE with CKPT_DIR named in the reason. The .gates attribute does survive -- but only because every Clock subclass in spine/units.py omits __slots__ and so gets an implicit __dict__; the docstring documents the arithmetic hazard and not that one. Suite is fully green, K13 included: the stub-count failure the previous agent reported as not-its-own has since been repaired.

findings.detail: D13's reversal of the frozen docstring's own 'q_entry and nov_proj stay, because both walks use them' rests on two factual claims, and both are wrong. (1) COUNT. The docstring says q_entry 'has exactly three readers' and names :2591, :2597, :2564. `grep -n q_entry self_organize.py` returns six reader sites: :2320 (route_w's non-grounded else), :2567 (seed_key's body; :2564 is the def line), :2591, :2597, :4019 (`fab.q_entry.in_features`, a shape read in fab_logits) and :9156 (the SPECIALIZATION probe). :2320 is a genuine forward-path read the ruling never mentions -- and the SAME LINE is one of the three sites the ruling cites in favour of KEEPING nov ('nov at :2361, :2320, :2580'), so the ruling counts one line as evidence for one name and does not see it for the other. (2) ARM. The docstring calls :2597 'the else of `if s.halt_on`, on that same non-grounded branch'. It is not on that branch. `cat -A` on self_organize.py:2588-2600 shows `_hlg = (...)` at eight-space indent, the same level as `if s.grounded:` -- it is evaluated after the grounded/non-grounded if closes, on BOTH branches, and its only gate is `s.halt_on`, i.e. FAB_HALT. FAB_HALT is not a dropped arm: .rework/census.json gives it verdict 'keep' with new_name FAB_HALT (contrast ROUTE_GROUNDED and FAB_DERIVE_IDS, both verdict 'drop'); src/fabric/levers.py::FABLevers.halt is Lever(True, ...); src/fabric/api.py::build reads it and writes counters['fab.halt']; src/fabric/api.py::forward names `halt` in LEVERS READ. So a q_entry reader is reached at ROUTE_GROUNDED=1 on the ported soc walk whenever FAB_HALT=0. THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES ANYWAY, on an argument D13 never makes: on the soc walk the pre-loop entry distribution `c` is consumed only by `s.ground_update(gist, c[:, :N], N)` (self_organize.py:2603) and the `if s.loop_soc:` block at :2619 returns at :2694 without touching it again; ground_update runs under `with torch.no_grad()` and renormalises (`_share = _iv / _iv.sum().clamp_min(1e-9)`, :2414), so a HALT-column logit -- which shifts every expert logit by the same softmax denominator -- changes neither the ranking nor the EMA rate. q_entry therefore has no gradient path and no numerical effect on the walk this tree ports, at either halt setting. That is the reason that holds; 'its readers belong to dropped arms' is not. Two supporting citations are also faulty: the old tree's 'never gradiented -> ctrl, q_entry' finding (self_organize.py:9141, audit loop at :7085) was measured at the shipped FAB_HALT=1 (self_organize.py:1734) and says nothing about the halt-off arm; and the two .rework/ISSUES.md records cited in the report as lines 1594-1595 and 1789-1790 are P3-C26 (cull budget) and P3-H28 (ACCUM) -- the SPECIALIZATION/q_entry records the ruling means are P3-C28 at 1602-1604 and P3-H30 at 1797-1799. The harm is that a frozen contract docstring now carries a false justification for reversing a dated ruling, and the next reader is P4, who writes forward(). If P4 ports the pre-loop entry distribution and gives it a live consumer, the FAB_HALT=0 arm needs a signature->dk projection that state_dict no longer names and build no longer allocates.

findings.detail: Attaching `.gates` to a units.Windows survives, and nothing about the Windows value breaks -- but the mechanism is an accident the ruling does not name. Clock declares `__slots__ = ("n",)`; Steps, Flushes, Windows, Backwards, Epochs and Selections declare a docstring and a KIND and NO __slots__ of their own, so Python gives every subclass instance an implicit __dict__ and `period.gates = (gate,)` succeeds. `'__slots__' in units.Windows.__dict__` is False; after the assignment `period.__dict__` is `{'gates': (...)}`. That means the whole D14 shape hangs on six subclasses each omitting a line that their base class declares -- the single most natural tidy-up anyone would make to that file (adding `__slots__ = ()` to the subclasses, which is what a slots-conscious author does) turns every compose() into an AttributeError at the `period.gates = (gate,)` line. save_period's docstring states the OTHER hazard carefully ('a Clock is a value object whose arithmetic returns a FRESH instance, so `period + Windows(0)` or a re-wrap `Windows(period)` drops the tuple') and says nothing about this one. Everything else checks out: int/__index__/bool/str/repr are unaffected, hash is still `hash((type name, n))` so a gated Windows hashes equal to a bare one, `==`, `>=` and `-` behave, `Steps(1) >= period` still raises UnitError, and `period == 0` still raises rather than silently comparing -- so carrying the tuple has not softened the one mechanism units.py exists for. The documented arithmetic cost is real and I reproduced it: `period - Windows(1)` returns a fresh Windows with no gates.

findings.detail: .rework/audits/todo/ckpt.json item 2 is closed exactly as its FIX NOTE asked and only half of what its TITLE asked, and the docstring says so itself, so this is a residue rather than a miss. The title is 'load raises on a missing resume file and never constructs a Resume, so the attempted-without-loaded state the record exists for is unreachable'. A Resume is now built and rides on Snapshot.resume -- verified with a synthetic checkpoint at step=555/epoch=2 with a best_state, which loads to Resume(attempted=True, loaded=True, step_restored=555, epoch_restored=2, best_restored=True). But `grep -n 'Resume(' src/ckpt/api.py` still finds exactly one constructor, at line 344, with attempted and loaded both hard-coded True, and the missing-file branch still raises FileNotFoundError (re-run against a nonexistent path: it does). So `Resume.attempted` and `Resume.loaded` are fields that can only ever hold one value, and the two-state distinction the class docstring says the record exists for ('attempted without loaded is the state the old tree could not report') remains unreachable. load's docstring names this in full, says why -- the raise means the run does not survive to print anything, and turning it into a printed state would reverse an already-settled refusal -- and refers the decision rather than taking it. That is the honest form. It is recorded here so the ledger does not read the todo item as closed on its title.

The halt_key bias=False change is the fifth question the referral did not name, and the reasoning holds, but it is a silent shape change to a module the tree had already allocated and it is worth having on the record. Old tree: `s.halt_key = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(dk) * 0.1)` at self_organize.py:1724 -- a BARE (dk,) key with no bias -- and the learned prior added separately at :2442 `torch.cat([logits, _hl + s.halt_b], -1)`. This tree had re-specified halt_key as nn.Linear(d_model, 1); a Linear's bias sits in precisely halt_b's additive position, so allocating both would put two learned scalars in one place with one necessarily dead. bias=False plus halt_b is a 1:1 match with the old tree's decomposition and the parameter count is unchanged. I confirmed `pop.modules['halt_key'].bias is None` and that halt_key contributes exactly one tensor (the weight) to the 20. Nothing contradicts it elsewhere: `grep -rn halt_key docs/ src/` finds halt_key nowhere in docs/04_CONTRACT.md and nowhere in src outside fabric/api.py, and .rework/census.json has no row for it. The residue is that FAB.load_state_dict is a stub and no checkpoint of this tree exists, so a shape change to an already-allocated module costs nothing today and would cost a refusal later; and that this tree's q_route (nn.Linear(d_model, dk)) and hproj (nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)) already differ from the old tree's (nn.Linear(sig_d, dk) at :1673 and nn.Linear(d, dk) at :1680), so 'built to the frozen old tree's own constructors' is a principle this file applies to the three new names and not to its pre-existing neighbours. That inconsistency predates D13 and is not its fault, but it does mean the old-tree geometry cannot be assumed transitive: the old halt-off expression at :2597, `(q_entry(gist) + nb) @ halt_key[:, None]`, is not even literally portable here, because this tree's halt_key is (1, d_model) and not (dk,).

The sentence that IS true and that carries the same conclusion: on the ported soc walk the pre-loop entry distribution `c` (self_organize.py:2600) reaches nothing but `s.ground_update(gist, c[:, :N], N)` at :2603, ground_update runs under no_grad and renormalises its top-k shares (`_share = _iv / _iv.sum().clamp_min(1e-9)`, :2414), and the `if s.loop_soc:` block returns at :2694 without reading `c` again -- so q_entry contributes no gradient and no number to the walk this tree ports, at FAB_HALT=1 and at FAB_HALT=0 alike. What would bring q_entry back is therefore not 'a non-grounded entry router' as the docstring says, but 'any live consumer of the pre-loop entry distribution', which is a strictly wider and more likely trigger -- P4 writing forward() with hop_sup or the vote fed from `c` would be one. Whoever fixes the docstring should also fix the 'returns to this list in the same commit that ports a non-grounded entry router' clause, because as written it under-describes the condition that would falsify the drop.

unfinished.title: units.Windows carrying .gates depends on six Clock subclasses each omitting __slots__, and nothing says so
unfinished.detail: src/spine/units.py::Clock declares `__slots__ = ("n",)` and its six subclasses declare none, which is the only reason `period.gates = (gate,)` in src/ckpt/api.py::save_period works. Adding `__slots__ = ()` to units.Windows -- the ordinary thing to do to a subclass of a slotted class, and something a future tidy-up or a memory pass would do without a second thought -- makes every compose() raise AttributeError on that line. The cost is one comment, either in units.py beside the subclasses ('these deliberately carry a __dict__; ckpt/api.py::save_period attaches a .gates tuple to a returned period') or as a second sentence in save_period's THE ONE COST paragraph, which today names only the arithmetic hazard. I do not own src/spine/units.py and may not edit either file.
